members.name: hull_ma_momentum_v1
members.thesis: The Hull Moving Average (HMA) with period 16 on 1-min bars provides a nearly zero-lag smoothed price signal by using weighted moving averages of different periods combined with a square root transformation. HMA(16) responds to price changes faster than EMA(16) or SMA(16) while maintaining smoothness
entry_long: HMA_slope_prev <= 0 (HMA just turned up — slope flip)
entry_short: HMA_slope_prev >= 0 (HMA just turned down — slope flip)
members.exit_stop: 0.2% from entry OR HMA_slope re-flips (direction reversal)
weaknesses: HMA(16) on 1-min bars responds to only 16 minutes of data — too short for meaningful trend detection in slow-moving stocks
The low-lag property means HMA also has more false flips than EMA — it is responsive to noise, not just signal
Conceptually, HMA is just a smoother MA — it does not provide fundamentally different information from other MAs, just earlier (noisier) signals
members.prior_art: Hull Moving Average by Alan Hull (2005). Designed to reduce lag in moving averages. Formula: HMA = WMA(2*WMA(n/2) - WMA(n), sqrt(n)). Less commonly used in Indian markets compared to EMA/SMA. Hull him

members.name: mean_reversion_hull_ma
members.thesis: Exploits the lag-less nature of Hull Moving Average (HMA). When price deviates too far from the 50-bar HMA and the HMA slope is flat, a reversion is imminent. Behavioral bias: traders see the price moving away and chase it, creating the extreme deviation required for the snap-back.
weaknesses: Requires high volatility to hit 1% deviation
